repo.name: node-express-realworld-example-app

critical_flows.name: Login and JWT authentication
critical_flows.business_impact: Establishes identity for every protected action. A bug here can lock all users out or allow account takeover.
failure_modes: Hardcoded 'superSecret' fallback if JWT_SECRET is unset allows forged tokens
observable_outcomes: 401 on protected routes without a valid token
preconditions: User exists with a bcrypt hash

critical_flows.name: User registration
critical_flows.business_impact: This is how users sign up. A bug can create duplicate accounts or store passwords incorrectly.
failure_modes: Race between the uniqueness check and create gives a 500
observable_outcomes: 422 when email or username is taken or blank
New User row with hashed password

critical_flows.name: Current user read and update
critical_flows.business_impact: Changes credentials (email and password). A bug can corrupt the account or let one user take another's email or username.
failure_modes: No uniqueness check on email or username, so a duplicate gives a 500
getCurrentUser on a deleted user crashes on null
observable_outcomes: 200 with updated user and new token

critical_flows.name: Article authoring (create, update, delete)
critical_flows.business_impact: This is the core content. Weak ownership checks would let users edit or delete other users' articles.
failure_modes: Tags are disconnected before the update with no transaction, so a failed update loses tags
observable_outcomes: 403 when the caller is not the author
preconditions: Article exists for update or delete

critical_flows.name: Article reading (list, feed, single)
critical_flows.business_impact: The main read path for all clients. A bug breaks browsing or leaks hidden content.
failure_modes: Visibility filter (demo or own) shows or hides the wrong content
Mapper crashes on a missing relation
observable_outcomes: 404 when the article is not found

critical_flows.name: Comments (add, list, delete)
critical_flows.business_impact: User discussion. A bug can let users delete other people's comments or create orphaned ones.
failure_modes: Nonexistent slug connects to an undefined article id, giving a 500
Comments outside the visibility filter are hidden
observable_outcomes: 404 when the comment is not the caller's

critical_flows.name: Social graph (favorite and follow)
critical_flows.business_impact: Engagement features. These drive the feed and favorite counts.
failure_modes: Unknown slug or username gives a 500 instead of a 404
observable_outcomes: Profile or article JSON with updated flags and counts

critical_flows.name: Popular tags
critical_flows.business_impact: Tag discovery in the sidebar. Low impact.

critical_flows.name: Database seeding
critical_flows.business_impact: Creates the demo content that anonymous users see.
failure_modes: Errors are swallowed in main, so the seed is partial and still exits 0
observable_outcomes: Demo users, articles and comments in the database

cruxes.name: generateToken
cruxes.why: Signs every JWT, and falls back to a hardcoded secret if JWT_SECRET is unset.
cruxes.risk_if_broken: Anyone can forge tokens and take over any account.

cruxes.name: login
cruxes.why: The single point where credentials are checked with bcrypt before a token is issued.
cruxes.risk_if_broken: Either every user is locked out, or anyone can log in without a valid password.

cruxes.name: getTokenFromHeaders
cruxes.why: Pulls the token out of the request for every route guarded by auth.required or auth.optional.
cruxes.risk_if_broken: Requests run with the wrong identity, or every authenticated request fails.

cruxes.name: createUser
cruxes.why: Hashes the password and saves the user. Registration and seeding both go through it.
cruxes.risk_if_broken: Passwords are stored in plaintext or wrongly, or invalid accounts are created.

cruxes.name: updateArticle
cruxes.why: Checks ownership, regenerates the slug and resets tags without a transaction.
cruxes.risk_if_broken: Users can edit other users' articles, or tags are lost.

cruxes.name: deleteArticle
cruxes.why: The ownership check that guards article deletion.

cruxes.name: deleteComment
cruxes.why: The comment ownership check. It filters by author and ignores the slug.
cruxes.risk_if_broken: Users can delete other people's comments.

files.summary: Core auth business logic: user creation, login, uniqueness checks, and password hashing. Critical for identity and account integrity.
JWT signing with hardcoded secret fallback. Generates every token issued to clients for authentication.
JWT extraction and middleware configuration. Guards every protected route with token validation and fallback secret.
Article and comment business logic: visibility rules, ownership checks, slug generation, tag management.
HTTP handlers for login, registration, and user profile. Entry points for F1, F2, F3 flows with delegation to service layer.
Transforms Prisma article data to API response format, computing favorited flag and flattening tags.
HTTP handlers for profile read and follow operations. Delegates to profile service.
Route handlers for article CRUD, comments, and favorites. Pass-throughs to service methods.
Express app setup, error middleware, and server startup. Routes all requests and handles errors.
Transforms author object to API response format, computing the following flag.
Profile queries and follow operations. Reads user and manages follow relationships.
Profile response mapper. Computes following flag and shapes profile output.
HTTP error wrapper that carries status code and error payload to all exception handlers.
Database seeding with generated demo users, articles, and comments. Creates initial content for F9.
HTTP handler for tag listing. Low-impact sidebar feature endpoint.
Retrieves top 10 popular tags filtered by demo and user. Low-impact read for sidebar.
Prisma client singleton initialization. Configuration plumbing for database access.
TypeScript interface definition for Article type.
Comment interface definition. Type definition for comment domain model used by comment endpoints.
RegisterInput interface definition. Input type for user registration endpoint.
RegisteredUser response interface. Output type for successful auth operations.
User entity interface definition. Domain model for user with relations to articles, comments, followers.
Profile response interface. Output type for profile endpoints with following flag.
Router aggregation. Combines all feature controllers under /api prefix.
Tag interface definition. Simple model for tag name.
Jest configuration preset that re-exports @nx/jest/preset for test runner setup.

method_analysis.name: login
method_analysis.why: Verifies credentials with bcrypt and issues JWT. Owns the single point where login can fail or grant access.

method_analysis.name: generateToken
method_analysis.why: Signs JWTs with secret or fallback. Token integrity failure disables all subsequent auth in F1, F2, F3.

method_analysis.name: updateArticle
method_analysis.why: Ownership check, slug regeneration, tag reset/update. Wrong logic lets users edit others' articles.

method_analysis.name: deleteArticle
method_analysis.why: Ownership check before deletion. Absence lets users delete others' articles.

method_analysis.name: deleteComment
method_analysis.why: Ownership check before comment deletion. Absence lets users delete others' comments.

method_analysis.name: createUser
method_analysis.why: Creates user with validated input, hashed password, and uniqueness check. Core transaction for account creation.
method_analysis.calibration_reason: Core user persistence; signing and login hold the true 10s

method_analysis.name: getTokenFromHeaders
method_analysis.why: Extracts JWT from request headers. Used by auth.required/optional middleware on every protected flow.

method_analysis.name: buildFindAllQuery
method_analysis.why: Encodes visibility rule (demo or own authors). Wrong logic leaks hidden articles or hides public ones.

method_analysis.name: createArticle
method_analysis.why: Validates input, generates unique slug, creates article with tags. Wrong logic creates duplicates or invalid articles.
method_analysis.calibration_reason: Persistence of core entity; no auth gate inside

method_analysis.name: router.post('/users/login')
method_analysis.why: Entry point for login. Delegates to login but is the HTTP door for F1.
method_analysis.calibration_reason: Pass-through door to login, one below callee

method_analysis.name: checkUserUniqueness
method_analysis.why: Enforces email and username uniqueness before user creation. Duplicate prevention is the crux guard for F2.
method_analysis.calibration_reason: Validation guarding a write; DB constraints likely backstop it

method_analysis.name: updateUser
method_analysis.why: Updates email, username, password without uniqueness check. Can corrupt accounts if email already taken elsewhere.

method_analysis.name: router.post('/users')
method_analysis.why: Entry point for user registration. Delegates to createUser but is the HTTP door for F2.

method_analysis.name: articleMapper
method_analysis.why: Used by all article responses. A bug in computed fields (favorited flag, tagList map) corrupts API output.

method_analysis.name: getArticles
method_analysis.why: Uses buildFindAllQuery to list articles. Defect would break browsing; logic lives in query builder.

method_analysis.name: getFeed
method_analysis.why: Reads feed for followed authors. A bug breaks personalized feed; read-only operation.

method_analysis.name: getArticle
method_analysis.why: Fetches single article. Defect would break article view; read-only query.

method_analysis.name: disconnectArticlesTags
method_analysis.why: Clears tags before update. A bug loses tag associations; used only during article update.
method_analysis.calibration_reason: Non-transactional tag wipe on article update path

method_analysis.name: getCommentsByArticle

method_analysis.name: addComment

method_analysis.calibration_reason: Core write of secondary comments flow

method_analysis.name: unfavoriteArticle

notes: Security: the JWT secret falls back to the hardcoded 'superSecret' in both auth.ts and token.utils.ts if the env var is missing.
Prisma client singleton (src/prisma/prisma-client.ts) and router mounting (routes.ts) are top-level code with no S-id, but every flow depends on them.
updateUser does not check email or username uniqueness, so a duplicate surfaces as a Prisma 500.
updateArticle clears tags, then updates, with no transaction. Favorite and follow on an unknown target return 500, not 404.
E21 is a mis-attributed bodyParser line that points at the GET / handler. It duplicates E20/E22.
Seed main swallows errors, so a failed seed can still exit with code 0.
The JWT secret falls back to the hardcoded 'superSecret'. If JWT_SECRET is not set in production, anyone can forge a token.
updateUser does not check that the new email or username is unique, so it relies on DB constraints for integrity.
updateArticle clears the tags and then updates the article outside a transaction. A partial failure leaves the article with no tags.
addComment does not check that the article exists, and deleteComment ignores the slug. Comment integrity relies on the DB.
buildFindAllQuery encodes the rule that decides which articles are visible. It stays at 8, but a regression there leaks hidden content.
